Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

military adjective and noun

of soldiers, war or the armed forces

also the military, military service, soldierly, in peace and in war, on the home front, military age, serviceman

classical

Liv. 21.4.7: mīlitārī sagulō
Caes. BG 1.21: rēs mīlitāris (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 345

mīlitāris, mīlitāre

Declension on Wiktionary

military, of soldiers

rēs mīlitāris, warfare, the art of war.

Other words

  • bellicus, bellica, bellicum — of war, warlike

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.78: bellicae laudēs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • mīlitia, mīlitiae f. — military service

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.55: domī mīlitiaeque (Lewis & Short); Traupman 187: in peace and in war, on the home front and the front line, domī et mīlitiae · Declension on Wiktionary

    domī mīlitiaeque, at home and in the field.

Examples

  • multī saepe mīlitārī sagulō opertum humī jacentem inter custōdiās statiōnēsque mīlitum cōnspexērunt

    many often saw him lying on the ground, wrapped in a soldier’s cloak, among the sentries and the picketsLiv. 21.4.7

  • quem mīlitārī vocābulō Caligulam appellābant

    whom they called by a soldiers’ nickname, CaligulaTac. Ann. 1.41

  • aetās mīlitāris

    military ageTraupman 187

See also army, soldier, war, battle, weapon, officer, campaign.
